title: Quick service restaurant chain Boba Bhai raises $18M in Series B round
summary: Quick service restaurant chain Boba Bhai raises $18 million in Series B round
detailed: Indian bubble tea and Korean street food brand Boba Bhai raised $18 million in a Series B funding round.
The round was led by new US-based investor Left Lane Capital and BIG Capital, alongside existing investor Titan Capital.
Boba Bhai and its founder Dhruv Kohli are involved alongside the funding partners.
This matters because the capital will be used for store expansion and scaling new food brands leveraging the company's existing operations and digital supply chain.
sentences: Boba Bhai, an Indian bubble tea and Korean street food brand, has raised $18 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Left Lane Capital and BIG Capital, alongside existing investors including Titan Capital.
According to a statement, the round brings US-based Left Lane Capital on board as a new investor, while BIG Capital is increasing its investment in the company.
Boba Bhai will use this funding round for store expansion and also scale up new brands under Boba Bhai Ventures.
Boba Bhai had previously raised Rs 40 crore in March 2026 from 8i Ventures, Titan Capital Winners Fund and Global Growth Capital, BIG Capital and angel investors.
Founded in 2023, Boba Bhai has 120 stores across the country and serves more than three lakh orders every month which include physical and digital channels.
Boba Bhai founder Dhruv Kohli said, “ Young Indian consumers are far more willing to experiment with global food formats today, but novelty alone does not build a lasting food brand.

What matters is whether you can deliver the same product and experience consistently as you scale.”
He further noted the experience over the last three years will enable them to expand further and also create new brands.
Boba Bhai has built its growth around a combination of bubble tea, Korean street food and fusion offerings, catering to young Indian consumers who are increasingly experimenting with global flavours.
The company has focused on product consistency, supply-chain discipline and store-level execution, while building its presence across physical retail, food-delivery platforms and quick commerce.
For the launch of new brands, this startup plans to use its existing capabilities across operations, supply chain, teams and digital distribution to launch and scale the concepts more efficiently.
Left Lane, the US-based consumer investment firm has backed food and consumer businesses across global markets including Blank Street Coffee and 7th Street Burger.
Boba Bhai is the fourth company in India to be backed by Left Lane Capital.
“We have tracked Boba Bhai's growth for over two years and have been consistently impressed by how Dhruv has built the business.

Boba Bhai stands out for its capital efficiency, its ability to quickly launch new concepts tuned to the local palate, and its relentless execution in delivering differentiated offerings for the Indian consumer,” said Arjun Kapur, Principal, Left Lane Capital.
